questions.prompt: Find the area scale factor of the linear map with matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&3\end{pmatrix}\).
questions.answer: In \(\mathbb R^2\), the absolute value of the determinant gives the area scale factor. The determinant is \(2\cdot3\) - \(0\cdot0\) = 6. Therefore areas are scaled by |6| = 6.

questions.prompt: Find the area of the parallelogram spanned by u = \((1, 2)\) and v = \((3, 4)\).
questions.answer: Place the vectors as columns of a \(2\times 2\) matrix: \(\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\2&4\end{pmatrix}\). The area is the absolute value of the determinant. Compute \(\\det=1\)*4 - \(3\cdot2\) = 4 - 6 = -2. Therefore the area is |-2| = 2.

questions.prompt: Find the area of the triangle with vertices \((0, 0)\), \((2, 1)\), and \((1, 4)\).
questions.answer: Use the two edge vectors from \((0,0)\): u = \((2,1)\) and v = \((1,4)\). The parallelogram area is |\(\det\left(\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&4\end{pmatrix}\right)\)| = |\(2\cdot4\) - \(1\cdot1\)| = |7| = 7. The triangle is half the parallelogram, so its area is 7/2.

questions.prompt: Find the volume scale factor of the linear map with matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&2&0\\0&0&-3\end{pmatrix}\).
questions.answer: In \(\mathbb R^3\), the absolute value of the determinant gives the volume scale factor. The matrix is diagonal, so \(\\det=1\)*2*(-3) = -6. The volume scale factor is |-6| = 6.

questions.prompt: Find the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by \((1, 0, 0)\), \((0, 2, 0)\), and \((0, 0, 5)\).
questions.answer: Place the vectors as columns of a \(3\times 3\) matrix. This gives the diagonal matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&2&0\\0&0&5\end{pmatrix}\). Its determinant is \(1\cdot2\)*5 = 10. The volume is the absolute value of the determinant, so the volume is 10.

questions.prompt: A \(2\times 2\) matrix has determinant -4. What does this say geometrically about areas and orientation?
questions.answer: The absolute value |det| = 4 gives the area scale factor, so areas are multiplied by 4. The negative sign means the transformation reverses orientation, such as changing a counterclockwise ordered basis into a clockwise one.

questions.prompt: A linear map in \(\mathbb R^2\) has determinant 0. What does this mean geometrically?
questions.answer: A determinant of 0 means the area scale factor is 0. The map collapses the plane into a lower-dimensional set, such as a line or a point. Therefore it is not invertible and does not preserve two-dimensional area.

questions.prompt: Find the area scale factor of the shear matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\).
questions.answer: Compute the determinant: \(1\cdot1\) - \(3\cdot0\) = 1. The area scale factor is the absolute value of the determinant, so it is 1. This shear changes shape but preserves area.

questions.prompt: The vectors u = \((2, 4)\) and v = \((1, 2)\) span a parallelogram. Find its area and interpret the result.
questions.answer: Place the vectors as columns: \(\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\4&2\end{pmatrix}\). The determinant is \(2\cdot2\) - \(1\cdot4\) = 4 - 4 = 0. The area is |0| = 0. This means the vectors are parallel, so they do not span a genuine two-dimensional parallelogram.

questions.prompt: A learner says determinant equals area, not signed area scale. Diagnose the error using \(\det\left(\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\right)\).
questions.answer: The determinant of \(\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\) is \(0\cdot0\) - \(1\cdot1\) = -1. An actual area cannot be negative. The absolute value |det| = 1 is the area scale factor, while the negative sign records orientation reversal. Therefore determinant is signed area scale, not simply area.
